layers.title: Layer 1 · Global architecture
layers.summary: Map of the system, global inconsistencies and the most urgent fixes.
items: Hours and time off approved only by Super Admins (migration 096)
Test pages out of the production build (they leaked sample data)
Donations and purchased hours can no longer be erased by a failed read
My Team tools read from the right table
Login page no longer shows text taken from the address
Dead code, em dashes and two unused libraries removed
Database types generated from the database itself (37 untyped clients removed)
layers.open: Items mapped but not approved were carried into the modules that own them.

modules.title: Login and session
highlights: Open redirect closed
Two-step and active/invited checked on every write
Session cookies httpOnly and secure
Limits on asking for and typing codes
A shared link survives two-step

modules.title: Access model
highlights: Teams and positions are Super Admin only
Nothing saves during a View Stage preview
Every access change and its log row in one transaction
Undo refused when something changed since
Access levels page split into seven files

modules.title: Navigation
highlights: View Stage keeps its preview everywhere, server redirects included
Search lists people without a link when their page does not open
Rail, search and drawer usable by keyboard
Every rail link checked against its page's guard, per level

modules.title: People
highlights: URGENT, fixed: the server move had reopened salaries, rates, personal contact and six server-only functions in the database (migration 098, in production)
Daily health check 'Database protections', in production and showing ok
One company mailbox per person: a login can no longer link to the wrong person (migration 099)
Removing someone with hours or rates makes them inactive, so reports stay true
Add person takes name and Work only; Personal and HR stay behind their own items
Team Leaders see active people only; the Directory list carries emails and Work only with their items
Every People and Teams action reports its real result, with portal confirmation dialogs
50 new tests, including what each viewer's person page reads
modules.note: In production (b06d54c). Three older screens (Projects progress, admin Settings, one action) use a query the new server refuses; fixes will be proposed in modules 10 to 12.

modules.title: Settings and notifications
modules.scope: Personal settings, notification rules, the daily summary email
modules.note: In production (747499a, migration 100). Health check now daily; all six checks ok.
highlights: Notifications and summary emails only for people active and invited
A failed read can no longer drop the day's summary emails
System notifications follow access items, not the level
Summaries claimed before sending: never twice, retries never double
Sign out everywhere and move to a new phone refused in View Stage
New health check "Daily summary email"; integrations checked daily
39 new tests, including the first ones for the summary run

modules.title: Clocky Hours and My Hours
modules.scope: Time clock, approvals, import from QuickBooks Time
modules.note: Skipped by your decision: the clock switch-over has not happened yet. Its 45 findings are kept for when it does.

modules.title: Client reports
modules.scope: i7 and Project Hours, PDF/CSV/image exports
modules.note: In production (ffe611d, migration 101). Kept as you decided: report holders still see per-person hours beside costs; every hour counts, approved or not.
highlights: Hand-added hours: the list no longer empties in 30-day months; a batch lands once; the panel touches only its own lines
A failed read shows as an error, never as $0 or the whole budget left
Invoice lines add up to their total, to the cent
Over budget prints as "over", in red; the client PDF waits for every rate
The Project Hours client file carries nothing internal
Rates start on the 1st; prepaid purchases keep a change history
26 new tests

modules.title: Report
modules.note: In production (b850e36, bde5867; migrations 102 and 103). 572 false hand-offs moved to a reserve table. Backlog column left as is: it clears on its own by about Nov 25.
highlights: Everyone, last 90 days: Delivered went from 0 (the log's first morning only) to 893 on staging
Hours over 13 weeks: 7,757h instead of the 2,442h the 1,000-row read saw
Held time in working days; late and today on the New York day
My team is the teams you lead; See everyone opens on Everyone; a filter is named everywhere
The person drawer opens, only for people your People tab lists
572 false hand-offs moved to a reserve table; repeats and hand-offs of finished steps ignored
21 new tests

modules.title: My Work
modules.scope: Monday work list, team priority, ingest
modules.note: In production (6826179; migrations 104 and 105). First production sync on the new code: 37 boards, no failures. The webhook check (S8) moves to module 11.
highlights: A bad Monday answer no longer empties a board
The change log and the board are written together
Work coming back after a setting is not announced as new
Monday tables are read by the server only
Two leaders editing one order get a warning instead of losing work
123 false events moved to a reserve table
37 new tests

modules.title: Publishing Goals
modules.scope: Publishing targets and the boards snapshot
modules.note: In production (8c3d434; migration 106). First production pull on the new code: both boards whole (AAAF 16,553 log entries, HFA 13,424); all 7 health checks ok.
highlights: The dashboard opens again for everyone with the tool
A partial Monday read keeps the good data
One busy month on AAAF had been cut at 10,000 entries: now read whole
Weeks in New York; targets judged by the week they applied to
Publishers editable in Settings; paused languages left out
Old Supabase login and editor removed from the dashboard
52 new tests

modules.title: SEO
modules.scope: Href Links (AAAF, HFA) and the coming-soon SEO tools
modules.note: Per-site access was removed on Oct 13: Href Links follows the tool's team setting, like every other tool (migration 109).
highlights: The overview counts again (it showed zeros since Oct 5)
The Monday webhook acts on what Monday says now and processes each delivery once
Links must be https on the site's own domain; hreflang code escaped
Per-site access applies everywhere
Recent activity from Monday shown, failures included
Href Links tables server-only

modules.title: Admin
modules.scope: Company settings, automations, inventories, system health
modules.note: In production (9ac9daf; migration 108). Crontab reinstalled: health every 4 hours; all 7 checks ok after the promote.
highlights: API tokens and the webhook secret server-only and Super Admin only
Token changes logged (who and when, never the value)
Health every 4 hours; could-not-run and long Monday silence count
One health summary for Automations and the Home banner, warnings in amber
Tickets retired; Tests checklist and the manual's Access section rewritten
Lint clean for the first time in the audit

still_open: Module 6, Clocky Hours and My Hours: skipped until the clock switch-over; 45 findings kept for it.
Three lesser join casts (my-team.ts, href-links data page names, report directory): typed reads, same fix as the three done.
The empty grants table: merge_people() still writes to it; it can go with the next change to that function.
Other reports (Full history export, Project Hours) still use the period popover; the i7 inline row can be reused there if wanted.
next_steps: Run the next audit when the clock switches from QuickBooks Time to Clocky, starting with module 6.
Keep "Database protections" green: any new server-only table or function goes into db_protections_check() in its own migration.
New pages keep passing coverage.test.ts, so a page never opens without its access check.
Changes keep the flow: staging first, then promote.
report_intro: From the architecture to each of the twelve modules, then a closing round of sixteen open items. Every change was approved by you, tried on staging first and then promoted to production. Nothing here is waiting for a decision.
report_footer: Audit of October 2026 · report written Oct 15, 2026
